title: Dynamic Motion Preverbs in Tactical Duels and Confrontations

sections.title: The Directional and Aspectual Functions of ki-, le-, and meg-
sections.content: You know preverbs with figurative meanings from B2 Unit 28. Preverbs attached to verbs of physical action create dynamic tactical predicates in Hungarian. The preverb 'ki-' denotes outmaneuvering or moving out of an opposing trap: 'kicselez' (to dribble/trick past), 'kivéd' (to parry/deflect away). Meanwhile, 'le-' adds the sense of getting the better of an opponent by outpacing them: 'leúszik' (to outswim/exhaust by swimming), 'lefut' (to outrun).

sections.title: Metaphorical Extension from Combat to General Life Strategy
sections.content: These sporting dynamic preverbs are routinely used in business, political debates, and intellectual polemics at the B2/C1 levels: 'kicselezi a bürokratikus akadályokat' (outmaneuvers bureaucratic hurdles), 'kivédi a kritikusok támadásait' (parries critics' attacks), and 'lefutja a versenytársakat' (outruns competitors).

sections.title: Dynamic Tactical Preverbs
rows: A vívó gyors mozdulattal kivédte a vágást.
The fencer parried the cut with a quick movement.
A csatár ügyesen kicselezte a védőt a kapu előtt.
The striker cleverly dribbled past the defender in front of the goal.
A pólósok könnyedén leúszták a fáradt ellenfelet.
The polo players easily out-swam the tired opponent.

items.spanish: A magyar kardozó minden támadást kivédett a döntő asszóban.
items.english: The Hungarian sabre fencer parried every attack in the deciding bout.

items.spanish: A vízilabdázók olyannyira felkészültek voltak, hogy a negyedik negyedben teljesen leúszták a rivális csapatot.
items.english: The water polo players were so well-prepared that in the fourth quarter they completely out-swam the rival team.

items.spanish: A tehetséges vívó ravasz cselekkel járt túl az ellenfele eszén a páston.
items.english: The talented fencer outwitted his opponent with clever feints on the piste.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Pay attention to object government: 'kicselez valakit' takes a direct accusative object (kicselezi a kapust), while 'kivéd egy támadást' takes the attack/shot as its accusative object.
